content.text:
Plan written to `redu-deploy-plan.md`. Here's what I propose:

## Filestash on redu — the plan

| | |
|---|---|
| **Image** | `machines/filestash@sha256:75d123c3…deb5808` (digest-pinned — the repo has no version tags) |
| **VM** | 1 × **m1.medium** (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB), `flavor_id "3"` |
| **Port** | 8334, behind an HTTPS access point |
| **URL** | `filestash-3ql7465g.redu.cloud` (generated up front — `APPLICATION_URL` must match exactly) |
| **Storage** | named volume on `/app/data/state/` (config, secret key, SQLite for share links + search) |
| **Database** | **none** — by design; your files stay on whatever storage you connect to |
| **Cost** | **GBP 0.0278/hr ≈ GBP 20.29/mo** — inside the no-card free trial |

**One deviation from what `plan_deploy` returned:** it quoted **m1.large at GBP 0.0486/hr (£35.48/mo)** because declaring a compose stack makes it assume an on-VM build. This is one pre-built container, and `redu.md` records m1.medium as correct — so I'll pass `flavor_id "3"` explicitly. That also keeps it inside the trial cap, which m1.large would break.

**Security work that is part of this deploy, not an extra:** a stock Filestash is an *unauthenticated admin console*. I've already generated a 32-char admin password and its bcrypt hash (60 chars, `$2y$12$`, verified against the password locally) — the hash goes in at deploy time, before the process listens. The moment `/healthz` says `pass` I'll set `middleware.identity_provider.type = admin` so the connect form asks for a password too, then run the verification script from `redu.md` before handing you anything. Dropping upstream's `collabora/code` service (loses in-browser Office editing only).

**Licence:** AGPL v3. Yours to self-host; §13 means if you offer it to others over the network you owe them the source of the version you run — the stock image satisfies that by pointing at upstream, which is why the digest is recorded.

content.text: Confirmed a genuine trap: Docker Compose expands `$Ue06…` in the `.env` value, silently truncating the hash to `$2y$12` — a 6-char `auth.admin` that nobody could ever log in against. Let me make the hash immune to it.

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-milos-Desktop-tests-lib-filestash/864cb794-fb60-4452-b706-b1c0caf47301/scratchpad
PW=$(cat admin.pw)
# Regenerate until the char after the 3rd '$' is NOT [A-Za-z_], so no '$' in the hash
# can ever look like a shell/compose variable reference under any quoting style.
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  H=$(htpasswd -bnBC 12 "" "$PW" | tr -d ':\n')
  C=$(printf '%s' "$H" | cut -c8)
  case "$C" in
    [A-Za-z_]) continue ;;
    *) printf '%s' "$H" > admin.hash; echo "found on attempt $i"; break ;;
  esac
done
H=$(cat admin.hash)
echo "length: ${#H}  char-after-3rd-\$: $(printf '%s' "$H" | cut -c8)"
python3 -c "
import bcrypt
print('bcrypt verify against password:', bcrypt.checkpw(open('admin.pw','rb').read(), open('admin.hash','rb').read()))"

cat > /home/milos/Desktop/tests_lib/filestash/verify-filestash.sh <<'EOS'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this Filestash is not an open admin console.
#   ./verify-filestash.sh filestash-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -u
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-filestash.sh <hostname>}"
H=$(mktemp); S=$(mktemp); C=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$H" "$S" "$C"' EXIT
XHR='X-Requested-With: XmlHttpRequest'

# 1. GATE. /healthz needs no headers and checks the config as well as the process.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$H" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/healthz")
case "$code" in
  502|503|504) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: proxy answered $code, the container is probably still starting. Re-run in two minutes."; exit 2 ;;
  200) : ;;
  *) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /healthz answered $code."; exit 2 ;;
esac
if ! grep -q '"status"' "$H"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200 but no status key. That is not Filestash answering."
  exit 2
fi
if grep -q '"status": *"transcient"' "$H"; then
  echo "FAIL the configuration sanity check is failing. Body:"
  cat "$H"; echo
  echo "     An admin.auth size that is not 60 means ADMIN_PASSWORD holds a plaintext password"
  echo "     rather than a bcrypt hash. Nobody can administer this instance. Redeploy with a hash."
  exit 1
fi
grep -q '"status": *"pass"' "$H" || { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: unexpected /healthz body: $(cat "$H")"; exit 2; }
echo "OK   /healthz says pass: [REDACTED:value] app is up, its config is readable, and the admin hash is 60 chars."

# 2. OWNERSHIP. Ask the question that actually matters: can an ANONYMOUS caller read the config?
sc=$(curl -sS -o "$S" -w '%{http_code}' -H "$XHR" "https://$HOST/admin/api/config")
grep -q '"status"' "$S" || {
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /admin/api/config answered $sc with no status key, so this proved nothing."
  exit 2
}
if grep -q '"result"' "$S"; then
  echo "FAIL an ANONYMOUS caller just read the entire configuration, which means auth.admin is"
  echo "     empty. The same caller can POST it back and own the instance. Take this down now."
  exit 1
fi
if grep -qi 'Not Allowed' "$S"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: refused by the origin check, not by the admin check. The X-Requested-With"
  echo "             header did not reach the app, so ownership was never tested. Fix and re-run."
  exit 2
fi
grep -qi 'Permission Denied' "$S" || {
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: unexpected refusal from /admin/api/config: $(cat "$S")"
  exit 2
}
echo "OK   an anonymous caller is refused with Permission Denied, so ADMIN_PASSWORD took effect."

# 3. THE FRONT DOOR. auth is [] exactly when no identity provider is configured.
cc=$(curl -sS -o "$C" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/config")
[ "$cc" = "200" ] || { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/config answered $cc."; exit 2; }
grep -q '"connections"' "$C" || { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/config has no connections key."; exit 2; }
nauth=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys
d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
print(len((d.get("result") or d).get("auth") or []))' "$C")
if [ "$nauth" = "0" ]; then
  echo "FAIL no authentication middleware is configured, so the connect form is open to anyone."
  echo "     They cannot read your files, but they CAN make this server dial any host they name."
  echo "     Set middleware.identity_provider.type to admin before handing this URL over."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK   an authentication middleware is configured: the connect form asks for a password first."

# 4. Prove the OUTCOME, not the status code: the admin password must actually sign in.
if [ -n "${FILESTASH_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  A=$(mktemp)
  printf '{"password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$FILESTASH_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
    | curl -sS -o "$A" -H "$XHR" -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/admin/api/session" >/dev/null
  if grep -q 'access_token' "$A"; then
    echo "OK   the admin password signs in and returns a token."
  else
    echo "FAIL the admin password does NOT sign in. The stored hash and this password disagree."
    echo "     Body: $(cat "$A")"
    rm -f "$A"; exit 1
  fi
  rm -f "$A"
else
  echo "note set FILESTASH_ADMIN_PASSWORD to also prove the password signs in. Do it before finishing."
fi
EOS
chmod +x /home/milos/Desktop/tests_lib/filestash/verify-filestash.sh

content.text:
## Filestash is live — closed, verified, and with one decision left for you

**https://filestash-3ql7465g.redu.cloud** · admin console at `/admin` · password `«REDACTED:entropy:142c8bfa»`

Deployment `465`, m1.medium (`flavor_id "3"`), **GBP 0.0278/hr ≈ £20/mo**, no database, image pinned to the digest in `redu.md`. `/healthz` says `pass`, and the admin password signs in and returns a token.

### Two things in `redu.md` turned out to be wrong, and both mattered

**1. The prescribed front-door fix does not exist in this image.** `plg_authenticate_admin` isn't compiled in — `GET /admin/api/middlewares/authentication` offers exactly `htpasswd, ldap, local, passthrough, wordpress`. Setting `identity_provider.type = admin` produces `trace=middleware not found` and gates nothing.

**2. The verification script's check #3 was a false pass.** It counted `auth` in `/api/config` and passed on any non-empty array — but a configured-yet-unbound identity provider makes that `[""]`, length 1. It reported "the connect form asks for a password first" while the instance was provably an open relay: I asked it to reach a black-holed private IP and **it hung for 45 seconds** opening a real socket, versus 0.08s against a refused port.

What actually gates outbound dialling is the `connections` allowlist. I emptied it. The same probe now refuses in 0.08s with `Not Allowed`, and every connector (`ftp/sftp/s3/webdav/git`) is refused without a socket. I rewrote check #3 to dial the black-holed IP and fail on a hang, so it tests behaviour rather than config shape.

### One trap caught before deploying

Your bcrypt hash would have been destroyed in transit. redu appends env values to the compose `.env`, and Compose expands variables there — a hash containing `$Ue06BI2l…` is a valid variable name, so it resolves to empty and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` arrives as the 6-character `$2y$12`. I reproduced it locally (Compose v5.3.1) before deploying, then regenerated a hash whose salt starts with a non-letter so it survives bare, single- and double-quoted `.env` forms alike.

### What you need to decide

The instance is closed, which also means **it cannot browse anything yet** — nothing is configured to browse, and choosing that needs your storage details. `redu.md` has a new "What is left to decide" section with both routes: one locked connection bound to the identity provider (recommended; `htpasswd` already holds an `admin` user with the same password), or restoring the seven default connectors and accepting the open connect form. Do it in the admin console — scripting `POST /admin/api/config` replaces the entire config file, wants plain values rather than the enriched shape it hands you, rotates `general.secret_key` if you omit it, and needs a container restart. I learned each of those by breaking the config twice; nothing was lost, since the instance was minutes old and holds no data of yours.

### Measured, since upstream publishes no number

Container idles at **60.9 MiB**, whole VM at 579 MB of 3916 MB, zero OOM kills, ~8 minutes to first healthy. **m1.small would have been enough** (£12.70/mo) for document browsing — the caveats are in-process thumbnailing/transcoding and `TMP_PATH` scratch on the VM disk, which m1.small halves to 20 GB.

Files updated: `redu.md` (10 new quirks, `last_deploy`, corrected prose, corrected embedded script), `redu-deploy-plan.md` (real provisioned values), `verify-filestash.sh`, `docker-compose.yml`. No credential is written to any of them. I applied the `last_deploy` and deploy-log edits by hand in redu's documented shape rather than re-posting the 29 KB file for a merge that only refreshes those two things — the quirks, which are the valuable part, are never written by the merge anyway. One recommendation for a future redeploy: set `CONFIG_SECRET`, which keys the encrypted identity-provider params independently of `general.secret_key`; I did not set it on this run.

## Fixed — that was my doing, and there was a second bug behind it

**Try https://filestash-3ql7465g.redu.cloud again:** you should get a login form. User `admin`, password `«REDACTED:entropy:142c8bfa»`.

**What broke it.** Emptying the `connections` allowlist closed the egress hole but left the front page with nothing to render: `ctrl_form.js` clamps its tab index to `0` and then renders `specs[0]` from an empty list. Undefined spec, client-side throw, internal error. I closed a security hole and shipped a broken page — I should have loaded the page after changing it rather than trusting the API-level checks.

**The second bug, which the fix uncovered.** Binding the login form to a connection got me a real password page, and the correct password was still refused as `Invalid username or password`. The cause: **the htpasswd provider rejects `$2y$` bcrypt hashes and accepts the byte-identical hash as `$2a$`.** I proved it by putting four users in one list — `$2y$` refused, the same hash re-prefixed `$2a$` accepted, along with `$apr1$` and even plaintext. It's the same hash `ADMIN_PASSWORD` accepts happily, because the console goes through `golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt` (which takes all three prefixes) while the plugin uses its own vendored `deps/crypt`. One hash, two code paths, different prefix support, and the failure looks exactly like a wrong password.

Then one more layer: with `related_backend` set but `attribute_mapping.params` empty, the right password authenticated and *then* died on `mapping_error - unexpected end of JSON input` — a failure that only appears after a successful login.

### Where it stands now

| | |
|---|---|
| Front page | htpasswd login form, renders in 200 |
| Correct password | authenticates → `is_authenticated: true` |
| Wrong password | `Invalid username or password` |
| Behind the login | `blackhole` — an inert placeholder that takes no hostname and serves a synthetic listing |
| Anonymous dial to any host | refused in **0s**, no socket opened (ftp/sftp/webdav/s3/git) |
| Admin console | works |
| `verify-filestash.sh` | 4/4, exit 0 |

The placeholder is the honest part: **it is not your storage yet.** Swapping it for real storage needs your credentials, so it stays your call — replace the single `blackhole` connection in the admin console and keep `attribute_mapping.related_backend` pointed at its label, and the login form stays in front of it.

`redu.md` now carries 36 quirks — four new ones from this round: the `$2y$`/`$2a$` split, the one-connection rule (empty allowlist is secure but unrenderable), the required `attribute_mapping.params`, and `blackhole` as the safe placeholder. The deploy log records plainly that the first handover was premature.
